title: Computer Security Technology Planning Study, Volume I
inherited_obligation: Every security-relevant reference must be mediated by an always-invoked validation mechanism.
action_chain_relation: Operation and control placement; principal–resource access check.
source_locator: PDF pp. 17–18 (report Sec. 4.1.1): reference monitor and reference-validation mechanism; footnote definition of all program references.
scope_limit: Establishes the reference-monitor concept, not a modern CUA implementation or performance claim.
canonical_citation: James P. Anderson. 1972. Computer Security Technology Planning Study, Volume I. Technical Report ESD-TR-73-51, Vol. I. Electronic Systems Division, Air Force Systems Command, L. G. Hanscom Field, Bedford, MA.
identity_note: The NIST-hosted PDF metadata and cover identify Volume I; this source fixes the volume used in the branch.

authors: Jerome H. Saltzer and Michael D. Schroeder
title: The Protection of Information in Computer Systems
foundation_family: Reference monitor / complete mediation; least privilege
inherited_obligation: Check every access to every object and restrict each program/user to the minimum privileges needed.
action_chain_relation: Complete mediation; technical permission, resource, and operation scope.
source_locator: Article Sec. I.A.3, PDF pp. 4–5: complete mediation and least privilege among the eight design principles.
scope_limit: Design principles are normative foundations; they do not by themselves define task authorization in natural-language agent workflows.
canonical_citation: Jerome H. Saltzer and Michael D. Schroeder. 1975. The protection of information in computer systems. Proceedings of the IEEE 63, 9 (September 1975), 1278–1308.
identity_note: DOI and journal citation match the selected canonical source; verification copy is a university-hosted reading copy.

authors: Jack B. Dennis and Earl C. Van Horn
title: Programming Semantics for Multiprogrammed Computations
inherited_obligation: Represent authority as explicit, operation-specific capabilities bound to protected objects.
action_chain_relation: Technical permission, protected resource, operation scope, and authority attenuation.
source_locator: MIT report PDF p. 12, Protection section: C-lists and capabilities locating segments and specifying permitted operations.
scope_limit: Provides capability semantics; it does not establish CUA-specific least-privilege enforcement.
canonical_citation: Jack B. Dennis and Earl C. Van Horn. 1966. Programming semantics for multiprogrammed computations. Communications of the ACM 9, 3 (March 1966), 143–155.
identity_note: The MIT technical-report text is used for locator verification; the canonical bibliography entry is the CACM version.

title: The Confused Deputy (or why capabilities might have been invented)
inherited_obligation: Keep delegated purpose and available authority distinguishable so a deputy cannot misuse its own privilege for an invoker.
action_chain_relation: Principal, authority source, delegated purpose, authorization basis, and permission scope.
source_locator: Article pp. 36–38; local PDF p. 2: authority stemming from two sources and the requirement to explicitly designate the authority used.
scope_limit: The paper supplies the authority-confusion mechanism; transfer to CUA scenarios requires a source-established acting principal and operation.
canonical_citation: Norm Hardy. 1988. The confused deputy (or why capabilities might have been invented). ACM SIGOPS Operating Systems Review 22, 4 (October 1988), 36–38.
identity_note: DOI metadata was verified; verification copy is an academic course-hosted copy.

title: A Note on the Confinement Problem
inherited_obligation: Constrain a service so protected information cannot escape through direct or indirect channels.
action_chain_relation: Protected information, disclosure effect, downstream reuse, and propagation.
source_locator: Article pp. 613–615; local PDF pp. 1–4: definition of confinement and transitive leakage channels.
scope_limit: Confinement concerns information leakage; it is not identical to incident containment after a harmful action.
canonical_citation: Butler W. Lampson. 1973. A note on the confinement problem. Communications of the ACM 16, 10 (October 1973), 613–615.
identity_note: DOI matches the selected canonical source; verification copy is an author-hosted copy.

title: A Lattice Model of Secure Information Flow
inherited_obligation: Enforce permitted information flows according to ordered security classes.
action_chain_relation: Source/target labels, permitted flow, disclosure, reuse, and propagation.
source_locator: Article pp. 236–243; local PDF pp. 1–3: lattice structure over security classes and secure-flow relations.
scope_limit: The lattice model supports flow constraints; CUA-specific labels and dynamic context remain a later synthesis.
canonical_citation: Dorothy E. Denning. 1976. A lattice model of secure information flow. Communications of the ACM 19, 5 (May 1976), 236–243.
identity_note: DOI and bibliographic details match the selected canonical source; verification copy is author-hosted.

authors: Martín Abadi, Michael Burrows, Butler Lampson, and Gordon Plotkin
title: A Calculus for Access Control in Distributed Systems
inherited_obligation: Represent principals, roles, and delegation explicitly when deciding whether a request is authorized.
action_chain_relation: Principal, delegated authority, speaks-for relation, authorization basis, and access decision.
source_locator: TOPLAS article Secs. 4–6; PDF p. 13, Sec. 5.1 'The Forms of Delegation': delegation as a primitive and its role in access decisions.
scope_limit: The calculus formalizes distributed authority; it does not directly encode natural-language task semantics or CUA trajectories.
canonical_citation: Martín Abadi, Michael Burrows, Butler Lampson, and Gordon Plotkin. 1993. A calculus for access control in distributed systems. ACM Transactions on Programming Languages and Systems 15, 4 (September 1993), 706–734.
identity_note: The 1993 TOPLAS version is retained; the earlier CRYPTO version is consolidated as a duplicate/version predecessor.

title: The UCONABC Usage Control Model
inherited_obligation: Evaluate and continue to enforce authorization using mutable attributes, obligations, conditions, and revocation.
action_chain_relation: Runtime constraints, mutable attributes, ongoing authorization, permission update, and revocation.
source_locator: Article abstract/introduction and authorization sections; local PDF pp. 1, 13–15: authorizations, obligations, conditions, continuity, mutability, and ongoing checks.
scope_limit: UCON supplies ongoing-control semantics; mapping user intent to attributes remains CUA-specific work.
canonical_citation: Jaehong Park and Ravi Sandhu. 2004. The UCONABC usage control model. ACM Transactions on Information and System Security 7, 1 (February 2004), 128–174.
identity_note: Author-hosted PDF and DOI match the canonical TISSEC article.

title: Guide to Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) Definition and Considerations
inherited_obligation: Make authorization decisions from attributes of the subject, object, requested operation, environment, and policy.
action_chain_relation: Principal attributes, protected resource attributes, operation, runtime context, policy, and authorization decision.
source_locator: NIST SP 800-162 Secs. 2.2–2.3, PDF pp. 16–18: subject, object, operation, environment conditions, policy, and decision/enforcement.
scope_limit: ABAC defines contextual authorization inputs; it does not establish which observed language constitutes user authority.
canonical_citation: Vincent C. Hu, David Ferraiolo, Rick Kuhn, Adam Schnitzer, Kenneth Sandlin, Robert Miller, and Karen Scarfone. 2014. Guide to Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) Definition and Considerations. NIST Special Publication 800-162, updated August 2, 2019.
identity_note: The updated August 2, 2019 NIST PDF is the canonical version used for source verification.

authors: Kiran-Kumar Muniswamy-Reddy, David A. Holland, Uri Braun, and Margo Seltzer
title: Provenance-Aware Storage Systems
inherited_obligation: Preserve lineage linking data and state to their producing events and ancestors.
action_chain_relation: Outcome evidence, state lineage, source provenance, and attribution inputs.
source_locator: USENIX paper abstract and Sec. 1, PDF pp. 1–2: automatic provenance/lineage collection and complete history/ancestry.
scope_limit: Storage provenance is an attribution prerequisite; it does not by itself establish responsibility or authorization.
canonical_citation: Kiran-Kumar Muniswamy-Reddy, David A. Holland, Uri Braun, and Margo Seltzer. 2006. Provenance-aware storage systems. In Proceedings of the 2006 USENIX Annual Technical Conference (USENIX ATC 06), 43–56.
identity_note: Official USENIX proceedings page and legacy paper PDF were preserved.

title: Guide to Computer Security Log Management
inherited_obligation: Collect, protect, review, and retain event records sufficient for monitoring and investigation.
action_chain_relation: Event record, actor/activity trace, outcome evidence, and auditability.
source_locator: NIST SP 800-92 Sec. 2, PDF pp. 9–15: logs as records of events and their operational, audit, and forensic uses.
scope_limit: Log availability does not guarantee semantic attribution or prove an external postcondition.
canonical_citation: Karen Kent and Murugiah Souppaya. 2006. Guide to Computer Security Log Management. NIST Special Publication 800-92.
identity_note: The 2006 final NIST guide is retained; the Rev. 1 draft is treated as a later draft, not the historical foundation.

title: Guide for Cybersecurity Event Recovery
inherited_obligation: Restore an acceptable state, validate recovery, and improve the recovery plan after a cybersecurity event.
action_chain_relation: External effect, resulting state, restoration, validation, and recovery status.
source_locator: NIST SP 800-184 Secs. 1.2–3 and recovery examples; PDF pp. 10–11 and 23–26: restoration, validation of recovery capabilities, and improvement.
scope_limit: The guide supports recovery obligations; it does not imply universal rollback of completed CUA actions.
canonical_citation: Michael Bartock, Jeffrey Cichonski, Murugiah Souppaya, Matthew Smith, Greg Witte, and Karen Scarfone. 2016. Guide for Cybersecurity Event Recovery. NIST Special Publication 800-184.
identity_note: Final NIST SP 800-184 is retained; presentation, bulletin, and draft versions are excluded as derivatives or predecessors.
